title: Preserve option-local choices, alternatives, variants, and prerequisites
description:
Repair known cases where source-defined choices/variants are absent, hoisted to a parent,
or flattened into cumulative behavior. Stable option identity/prerequisites are required
where runtime consumers reference them. A structural option family may be exhaustively
checked only when membership is independently source-enumerated.
design:
2026-10-10 DESIGN (Claude Captain, main 16eea662). Lane A, profile rules-clause-complete. Split: implementation child = O1-O4 (parser repairs + cross-kind siblings); Captain = registry dispositions O5-O8 in the same PR.
O1 ALTERNATIVE-ABILITY SAVE (opus:F-33 bulette-alternative): creature:bulette Deadly Leap prints 'must succeed on a DC 16 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (target's choice)' but projects saves [{ability:'dexterity', damageOnSuccess:'half'}] - the Strength alternative and the DC are lost. Representation: a save may carry abilityOptions: ['strength','dexterity'] (exactly the printed abilities, in printed order) plus chosenBy: 'target' (from '(target's choice)'; omit chosenBy if not printed) INSTEAD of ability, with its dc and success branch. Validate in kindSchemas: exactly one of ability | abilityOptions (>=2 distinct abilities). BEFORE emitting, grep packages/core/src for every consumer of mechanics saves[].ability; if any consumer requires ability, stop and report. Population by query across ALL kinds: '<Ability> or <Ability> saving throw' (with or without a DC); repair every sibling or disposition it with a source reason.
O2 PIT VARIANTS (opus:F-02): hazard:pits flattens four printed traps (Simple Pit, Hidden Pit, Locked Pit, Spiked Pit) into one record whose mechanics carry only the Spiked Pit poison variant's save (DC 13 Con half, 4d10 poison) plus the spikes' 2d10 piercing - read as if every pit poisoned. Representation: data.variants = [{name, text (verbatim span of that trap's paragraph), mechanics?}] one per printed trap, each with only its own projections (detection/investigation DCs as the existing check grammar yields them, Locked Pit's Strength check DC, Spiked Pit's 2d10 piercing and its poison clause DC 13 Constitution half 4d10 poison); top-level mechanics keep only what applies to every pit (falling damage by depth is prose: leave it unprojected unless the existing grammar already projects it) - in practice top-level mechanics should become absent or contain nothing variant-specific. The record's description stays verbatim. Validate variants in the hazard kind schema (reuse the creature variant shape {name, text, mechanics?}). Check consumers of hazard mechanics (grep) first; stop and report if a deterministic consumer exists. Sibling search: other hazard/trap records that print several named sub-traps in one record; repair or disposition.
O3 CROSS-KIND DAMAGE ALTERNATIVES (opus:F-27): creature attack alternatives are repaired in PR #646 (attacks[].alternatives). Search spell, magic-item, equipment, hazard, feature text for the same printed grammar (', or N (XdY) <type> damage <condition>' or 'deals XdY ... or XdY ... if/when ...' alternatives) whose projection lists both as cumulative damage; repair with the same alternative representation where a damage list exists, or disposition each with a source reason. Equipment 'versatile (1d10)' is already typed as a property - verify, do not re-model.
O4 CROSS-KIND TARGETING QUALIFIERS (opus:F-35): creature attack targets are repaired in PR #646. Search other kinds' projected target fields (spells' target text if projected, magic-item effect targets) for truncation of a printed qualifier; repair or disposition.
EVIDENCE: one new test file: exact bulette save; a generalized invariant over all records that every '<A> or <B> saving throw' clause projects abilityOptions [A,B] (independent regex); exact pits variants (four names, Spiked Pit alone carries the poison save); cross-kind dispositions listed in bead notes (not tests) unless a repair was made.
Registry (implementation child): bulette-alternative (F-33) and pit-variants (F-02) stay accepted with repair reasoning; damage-alternatives (F-27) and targeting-qualifiers (F-35) get reasoning citing PR #646 for creatures plus this PR's cross-kind result. Captain handles invocation-effects (F-07), choice-behavior (indep:002), language-universe-policy (indep:011), option-losses (CAP-005).
acceptance_criteria:
- A selected represented option grants only its own source-backed behavior; sibling alternatives are not cumulative.
- Stable identity/prerequisites exist for represented options consumed by discovery, state, or capabilities.
- Open-ended source choices remain open rather than falsely closed.
- Exhaustive predicates name an independently source-derived option family.
- Capability execution, tool exposure, and state effects are out of scope here; they belong to the capability lane (eshyra-o9bd.19.5 family epics, eshyra-olc5.1/.2).
notes:

regression predicate + committed assertions, generated outputs, no-repeat alias
list, and completion proof. "Fix the examples above" is not acceptable scope;
close the whole semantic class and reconcile exact membership.

DESIGN ADDITION O5 (Claude Captain 2026-10-10, main 16eea662): OPTION-PROSE HOISTED TO PARENT (indep:002 choice-behavior / opus:F-07 class). feature:warlock:pact-boon carries parent-level mechanics.spellGrants [spell:find-familiar], but only the Pact of the Chain option grants it (Blade/Tome do not). Root cause: deriveFeatureMechanics runs on the parent's full text, which includes every option's prose. No runtime consumer reads feature spellGrants (grep), so this is source projection read by discovery/DM. Closure: for every feature whose record carries option-catalog choices (choices[].options or data.optionCatalog), parent mechanics must not contain projections derived only from an option's text; derive parent mechanics from the parent's own (non-option) prose, and move option-specific projections to that option (option.mechanics) only where the existing schema/consumers support it (spellGrants on Pact of the Chain is the expected case), otherwise leave them in the option's verbatim text. Population by query over all features with options; list every parent whose mechanics change. Evidence: generalized invariant that no parent mechanics projection is derivable only from option text (independent check: each parent projection's source phrase occurs in the parent's non-option prose), plus exact Pact Boon assertion.
CAPTAIN DISPOSITIONS (planned 2026-10-10, applied at integration; verified on main 16eea662): (F-07 invocation-effects) accepted, repaired: feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations carries no parent mechanics; the only option mechanics are Beguiling Influence's typed proficiency grant (eshyra-olc5.7, PR #642); hoisting removed by eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1.3.1 (PR #569). (indep:002 choice-behavior) accepted, repaired by O5 in this PR (parent mechanics no longer carry option-only projections; Pact Boon find familiar) plus existing option-keyed procedures (fighter fighting-style feature-options procedure keys each effect by option id). (indep:011 language-universe-policy) STILL LIVE: background/ancestry language choices are closed to the 8 Standard Languages (e.g. background:acolyte languages from[8], 'Two of your choice'), but rule:languages also allows 'one that is common in your campaign' and, with GM permission, Exotic or secret languages. Repair needs a creation consumer change (GM-approved extension) in ancestry/background projection territory -> RE-OWN the row to eshyra-o9bd.19.3.3 (the July defect map already assigns indep:011 there) with reasoning stating it is open; add the obligation to 19.3.3. (CAP-005 option-losses) narrowed: the original example list is not recorded in the repository; the surviving obligation is that no source option/choice/progression region is dropped, enforced by the source-region ledger coverage gates and the level-up choice coverage invariant (levelUpChoiceCoverage.ts), with October instances repaired by PRs #569, #613, #617, #631; any newly found loss is a new finding.
DESIGN ADDITION O3b (Captain 2026-10-10): spell:fire-shield ('2d8 fire damage from a warm shield, or 2d8 cold damage from a cold shield') and spell:spirit-guardians ('3d8 radiant damage (if you are good or neutral) or 3d8 necrotic damage (if you are evil)') project cumulative [fire, cold] / [radiant, necrotic]. These are ONE damage roll whose TYPE is an alternative. Representation: a single damage entry {dice, typeOptions: [{type, condition: <verbatim>}, ...]} in place of the two entries; if the pack already has a spell damage shape for a chosen/alternative type (grep typeChoice in kindSchemas and records for spells such as chromatic-orb), reuse it and add only the verbatim condition. Validate (exactly one of type | typeOptions; >=2 distinct canonical types). Consumer check first: grep packages/core/src for readers of spell mechanics.damage (spell upcast transform in particular); if a deterministic consumer reads damage[].type, update it to handle typeOptions without inventing a type, or stop and report. Sibling sweep over all spells (and magic items) printing 'N <type> damage ... or N <other type> damage <condition>' with a cumulative projection; repair each. eshyra-513u closed as absorbed.
